lesson_title: The Vetkoek Line: Reconciliations, Costing and VAT, Revised
hook_text: Vetkoek 1 to 499 work for the landlord. Number 501 works for YOU.
clip_script: A vetkoek stand. Each one sells for twenty-five rand; the flour, oil and filling cost ten. So every vetkoek sold carries fifteen rand toward the fixed life of the stand — the rent and the gas contract, seven and a half thousand a month whether you fry one or a thousand. Now the only question that matters: how many vetkoek until the rent is paid? Seven and a half thousand divided by fifteen — five hundred. Vetkoek one to four ninety-nine? Working for the landlord. Number five hundred squares the month. And number five-oh-one is the first one working for YOU — from there, every vetkoek drops its whole fifteen rand in your pocket. Sell six hundred and twenty, and the hundred and twenty past the line make eighteen hundred rand of pure profit. And watch this: cut your price to twenty-two, and the line jumps to six hundred and twenty-five. Cheaper is not automatically smarter. That line has a name — break-even — and finding it is the difference between working for the landlord and working for yourself.
visual_style: A sizzling pan counting vetkoek as they fly onto a number line; the first 499 tinted grey and stacking under a landlord's door, number 501 turning gold; the line visibly sliding right when the price tag drops to R22.
mood: Street-smart and empowering — business maths you can feel.
pacing: Setup sizzle, the countdown to 500, the golden 501 beat, the price-cut twist.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision session and find your own line.
